To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have mapped and characterized the non-thermal emission from the northwest region of the supernova remnant (SNR) RCW 86, which is dominated by synchrotorn radiation.

(1) we detect non-thermal X-rays from the northwest region of supernova RCW 86, (2) the magnetic field in this region is amplified to approximately 100 μG, and (3) we find that the magnetic field is not amplified by the presence of cosmic rays.

we detect a narrow, filamentary, non-thermal X-ray emission region in the northwest region in RCW 86, that is spatially correlated with a radio filament, and that the width of the filament is consistent with the synchroton cooling length of the X-ray emission.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the physics of particle acceleration in the northwest region, and the magnetic field structure in RCW 86, which will be useful for the interpretation of future observations of supernova remnants with the next-generation gamma-ray telescopes.
